rationale.en: A Berkeley Research Group report (November 2025), using data supplied by the California Primary Care Association, estimates about $1.7 billion in penalties by the clinic organizations studied in the first year. The Analyst says the affected clinics currently report spending an average of about 80 percent of revenue on health care services, that the penalty equals the spending needed to reach the 90 percent minimum, and that clinics get the money back if they comply within five years. So the $1.7 billion is a payment to the state that can be recovered, not a loss of funding.
